An agent scoring 0.60 on single attempts would sit near 0.08 on five trials if they were independent.

Reliability in support agents should be measured by running tasks multiple times to see if they consistently follow policy, rather than relying on single-attempt success rates. The support agent benchmark runs every task "five times".

A task passes only when the final state, tool usage, and policy adherence all hold. The backend is designed to permit policy violations so that the agent's adherence can be tested.

In the current run, 29 of 37 state-changing calls occurred after the simulated customer had left. The evaluation harness uses two fixture tasks, oracle and mute, which must score 1.000 and 0.000 respectively to ensure the scoring logic remains valid.

The evaluation suite consists of twenty hand-written tasks rather than tasks sampled from real support logs. Run that task once and you learn whether the agent can do it; run it five times and you learn whether it can be relied on.
